coord_notes.kind: A \(T\)-point over token positions: \(a(i)=q\) on prompt positions \(i\le\ell\) and \(a(i)=q_0\) on generated positions, so \(\rho\circ a\) takes only the values \(W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA\) and \(\theta_0\). It is aLoRA's position gate mirrored: on for the prompt, off for decoding.
coord_notes.shape: No single weight-space image: prompt and decode positions see different weights, and generated tokens feel the adapter only through the cached \((K,V)\) of positions \(\le\ell\). Compared through the realisation \(\Phi\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(\mathrm{LoRA}_P\) keeps \(B_0=0\): the frozen function at every position, with first-order image \(\{XA_0\}\) on prompt positions (\(\mathrm T_A\) apex, as aLoRA). \(\mathrm{DiReFT}_P\) at its released init (\(W_1=0\), \(b=0\), orthonormal \(W_2\)) is a neutral residual-stream box, also first-order deficient (only \(W_1,b\) move).
coord_notes.gauge: \(\mathrm{LoRA}_P\): \(GL_r\) on the single adapter. \(\mathrm{DiReFT}_P\): \((W_2,W_1,b)\mapsto(gW_2,\,g^{-\top}W_1,\,g^{-\top}b)\), again \(GL_r\).
coord_notes.covariance: On each prompt position the update is LoRA's basis-free cone (\(\mathrm{DiReFT}_P\): a dense rank-\(r\) affine edit of the residual wire): function-level \(GL\times GL\).
coord_notes.merge: Thm VI.3(a): a position-gated edit has no position-independent weight. Prefilling with a merged copy and decoding with \(W_0\) uses two weights; it is not a merge.
coord_notes.rebasing: Undefined: nothing merges into the base (M\(\infty\)).

methods.categorical_reading: PreFT is LoRA (or DiReFT) pulled back along the prompt-position gate, the mirror image of aLoRA's gate: a family \(T\to Q\) that sits at \(q\) on positions \(\le\ell\) and at \(q_0\) afterwards. Under causal attention the generated tokens see the adapter only through the prompt's \((K,V)\) cache, so the realised map is not \(\Phi_f(\theta)\) for any single \(\theta\). Being pointed after \(\ell\) is what lets decoding run on the frozen weights, and also what blocks merging.

arrows.note: DiReFT_P instance, into LoReFT intervening at every prompt position (prefix length >= ell) after every block: s_r W_2^T(W_1 h + b) = R^T((W - R)h + b'). Smooth where W_2 has full row rank. Pointed: the released init (W_1 = 0, b = 0, W_2 with orthonormal rows) goes to LoReFT's neutral point W = R, b = 0. Checked numerically (error 2e-16). The target is LoReFT pointed at its neutral point (W = R, b = 0), not at pyreft's default init, which is a defect.

obstructions.reason: At function level the realised map (adapted prompt KV cache, frozen decode weights) is not Phi_f of any single weight for generic prompts, so no weight-space LoRA lifts it (M-infinity). On each prompt position the update is still a LoRA update.

Complementary gates on the same LoRA update. For a fixed invocation position aLoRA leaves the prompt before t_inv at W_0 and adapts later tokens; PreFT adapts the prompt and leaves every generated token at W_0. For generic prompts neither family of realised maps contains the other.

coord_notes.kind: Post hoc and training-free: OFT rotations \(R_i\) (or Procrustes rotations of other experts) go to \(Q_i\in\mathfrak{so}(d_{in})\) by the inverse Cayley map, are averaged with the norm-restoring factor \(c=\sum_i\|Q_i\|_F/\|\sum_iQ_i\|_F\), and come back by the Cayley map.
coord_notes.shape: No tunable coefficient in the OFT-expert rule (uniform \(1/N\), \(c\) fixed by norms), so the output is a single point (post-hoc convention). It is the point \(Q_m\) of the orbit chart \(Q\mapsto W_0C(Q)^{\top}\). For non-OFT experts the residual rule (TA's \(\lambda\)) adds a coefficient line.
coord_notes.base_point: A single point that does not arise from a coefficient value at \(\theta_0\); generically \(\neq\theta_0\), as for soups and RegMean.
coord_notes.gauge: No trained coefficients. Read as the family \(\lambda\mapsto W_0C(\sum_i\lambda_iQ_i)^{\top}\), it would be injective near 0 for independent \(Q_i\).
coord_notes.covariance: OFT experts: \(W_0\mapsto gW_0h^{-1}\) conjugates every \(R_i\) by \(h\in CO(d_{in})\) (block normaliser for block OFT), and the Cayley map, the average and the Frobenius norms commute with that conjugation: \(GL\times CO\), as OFT. The Procrustes instance needs \(g\) orthogonal too (\(CO\times CO\)), and a TIES residual rule cuts it to monomials.
coord_notes.merge: \(W_0R_m^{\top}+\rho_m\) is an ordinary weight.
coord_notes.rebasing: A one-shot post-hoc operation.

methods.categorical_reading: OrthoMerge is task arithmetic in the Cayley chart of the orbit \(W_0\cdot SO(d_{in})\) rather than in \(T_{\theta_0}\Theta\). The merged point \(W_0C(Q_m)^{\top}\) stays in the \(K_{\rm out}\) level set that every OFT expert preserves, which no linear merge of OFT experts does. For non-OFT experts it first splits each weight into an orbit point and a residual, merges the two parts by the orbit rule and by a Euclidean rule, and adds them.

arrows.note: OFT experts sharing one block partition, exact Cayley on both sides: the merged point is a point of OFT's image (unpointed slice, as soups into task arithmetic). With OFT written as W_0 C(Q)^T, C(Q) = (I+Q)(I-Q)^{-1} (OrthoMerge's own convention), h(*) = Q_m; under HF's R = (I-Q)(I+Q)^{-1}, h(*) = -Q_m. Experts trained with HF's default Cayley-Neumann map are read through exact Cayley only approximately.

obstructions.reason: For N >= 2 OFT experts with generic generators, W_0(C(Q_m)^T - I) is not in span{W_0(C(Q_i)^T - I)}, because the Cayley map is not linear. Conversely task arithmetic's family leaves the K_out level set that OrthoMerge's output keeps.

coord_notes.kind: An optimizer-only change on a LoRA-type object. Per-example gradients are projected onto \(T_{BA}\mathcal M_r\), clipped and noised there, lifted canonically to the factors and retracted. The parametrisation is the released spectral-residual one.
coord_notes.shape: Released init (spectral_init_peft_model): \(W_{\rm res}=W_0-[W_0]_r\) with \(sB_0A_0=[W_0]_r\), so the image is PiSSA's translated cone \(W_{\rm res}+\mathcal M_{\le r}\). The tangent projectors need full-rank factors, which rules out LoRA's \(B=0\) apex: a Type II start is forced.
coord_notes.base_point: S stratum: \(\theta_0\) is a smooth point, \(\dim S_1=r(m+n-r)\).
coord_notes.gauge: The object's gauge is \(GL_r\). Clip, noise and step depend only on \(\mathrm{col}\,B\), \(\mathrm{row}\,A\) and \(\mathcal P_{B,A}(G)\), so the randomised update, noise included, descends to the quotient \(\mathcal M_r=Q^{\rm full}/GL_r\). LoRA-RITE's descent covers only the deterministic step.
coord_notes.covariance: The init frame is a truncated SVD of \(W_0\) (\(CO\times CO\), Prop II.16). The Frobenius tangent projection and the isotropic Gaussian noise are \(O\times O\)-equivariant (in law).
coord_notes.merge: The code saves the adapter on the original \(W_0\) as the rank-\(2r\) pair \([B,B_0][A;-A_0]\), an ordinary LoRA that fuses.
coord_notes.rebasing: As PiSSA: \(\to\Theta\).

methods.categorical_reading: PRISM keeps PiSSA's object and moves DP-SGD from \(Q\) to the base \(\mathcal M_r\) of the gauge bundle \((B,A)\mapsto BA\). Clipping and noise act on the tangent projection \(\mathcal P_{B,A}(G)\), so the whole randomised step, noise included, is a function of \(BA\), and the bilinear \(\eta^2\xi_B\xi_A\) term of factor-space DP disappears. It is the stochastic counterpart of the descended cometrics of Exposé III (LoRA-Pro's projected gradient, Riemannian preconditioning).

arrows.note: Isomorphism onto PiSSA_r (scale 1) on the same residual W_0 - [W_0]_r. It sends PRISM's q_0 = (U_r(Sigma_r/s)^{1/2}, (Sigma_r/s)^{1/2}V_r^T) to PiSSA's (U_r Sigma_r^{1/2}, Sigma_r^{1/2}V_r^T). Only the optimiser differs. Checked numerically.

coord_notes.kind: Per task, LoRA with a designed frozen \(A_t\) and a trained \(B_t\), re-based so that the start reproduces \(W_{t-1}\); the branch is merged after each task.
coord_notes.shape: \(W'+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA_t=W_{t-1}+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}(B-B_t^{(0)})A_t\): the linear space \(W_{t-1}+\mathbb R^{d_{out}}\otimes\mathrm{row}\,A_t\), \(d=rd_{out}\), with \(\mathrm{row}\,A_t\perp[P_W,M_{t-1}]\).
coord_notes.base_point: Linear and injective, hence regular. The offset \(B_t^{(0)}=U_rS_r\) is absorbed by \(W'\) and changes neither the image nor \(S_1\).
coord_notes.gauge: None: \(A_t\) has orthonormal rows.
coord_notes.covariance: \(P_W\) is a truncated-SVD frame of \(W_0\), and \(A_t\) is the top right singular subspace of a projected gradient (LoRA-GA's frame type): \(O(m)\times O(n)\), scale-invariant. The past-feature basis \(M\) is a data frame on the input side.
coord_notes.merge: Each task's \(\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B_tA_t\) is folded into \(W\).
coord_notes.rebasing: One stage per task with a moving designed frame (InfLoRA's scheme). Each stage alone is idempotent; after \(T\) tasks the reach is \(W_0+\{X:\mathrm{row}\,X\subseteq\sum_t\mathrm{row}\,A_t\}\).

methods.categorical_reading: KeepLoRA is LoRA-FA re-based once per task. Its frozen frame comes from the SVD of the first-step gradient after the principal input subspace of \(W_0\) and past-task features have been projected out. By the degree-one collapse each stage is full fine-tuning projected onto \(\mathrm{row}\,A_t\), so \(\Delta W\,[P_W,M_{t-1}]=0\) by construction. The nonzero \(B_t^{(0)}\) is a split pointing of a linear method, so it changes only the parametrisation.

arrows.note: Per task: LoRA-FA(A_t) over the base W_{t-1} (same scale), pointed at 0. Checked numerically.
Per task, into LoRA pointed at (0, A_t), a T_A point with orthonormal A_t (composite with FA(A_t) -> LoRA).

obstructions.reason: Per task both are FA-type linear spaces, but KeepLoRA's row A_t comes from a projected-gradient SVD and InfLoRA's from projected activations. For generic data the row spaces differ, so the stage images are not nested.

coord_notes.kind: Forward map \(\mathrm{id}_\Theta\). The weight step is Adam's (or Muon's) full step; only the EMA moments are stored as rank-\(r\) factors, updated by closed-form Newton steps. In the cotangent table it shares Flora's row (compress only the optimiser state), with learned instead of random factors.
coord_notes.shape: \(M_t=\beta_1m_Bm_A+(1-\beta_1)G_t\) contains the raw gradient and the Adam ratio is elementwise (Muon: \(\mathrm{NS}_5\) of a full-rank matrix), so one step can move in any direction: the per-step image is \(\Theta\) (Lin, \(d=\dim\Theta\), as Fira and APOLLO).
coord_notes.base_point: No reparametrisation: training starts at \(\theta_0\).
coord_notes.gauge: \(\rho=\mathrm{id}\). The factored state has its own \(GL_r\) redundancy \((m_Bg^{-1},gm_A)\), and the Newton factor updates respect it; that is a symmetry of the optimiser state, not of \(\rho\).
coord_notes.covariance: The image is \(\Theta\), so \(GL\times GL\). The update rule itself is only Mon\(\times\)Mon (elementwise Adam ratio).
coord_notes.merge: Writes \(W\) directly; nothing to merge.
coord_notes.rebasing: Null: LoRA-Pre takes full-space steps and compresses only its moments, so it has no per-period shape to merge and restart. This is Flora's row in Exposé VIII.B (rebasing '–') and conventions deviation (3) of theory/axes.json, which gives exactly this reason for nulling Flora's rebasing.

methods.categorical_reading: LoRA-Pre is Full FT with a compressed optimiser state. Its object is the terminal \((\Theta,\theta_0,\mathrm{id})\); the low rank lives only in the momenta, which are themselves trained as an online low-rank regressor of the gradient stream. Unlike GaLore, whose step is confined to a moving rank-\(r\) period, nothing confines its update, and every difference from Adam lies in the induced cometric.

arrows.note: Both are the terminal object with forward map id_Theta; they differ only in optimiser data (Def III.1).

coord_notes.kind: Read with the released transform: merge_structlora merges the coordinator output \(u_l+\mathrm{Dec}(H_l)\), with \(u_l=\mathrm{vec}(\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B_l\,\mathrm{diag}(m_l)A_l)\) and \(H\) a one-layer residual GCN over the encoded \(u_l\). Sec. 3.3 agrees; App. E.7 says instead that the gated update is merged.
coord_notes.shape: One GraphCoordinator serves all adapted matrices, and its decoder \(\mathrm{Dec}(z)=Dz+c\) is a trainable dense map into \(\mathbb R^{\max d_{out}d_{in}}\) (checked in the released coordinator.py). The bias \(c\) translates every box freely, and \(D\) moves the boxes independently when the \(H_l\) are linearly independent (at most 128 boxes). So the reachable set is all of the adapted boxes, a flat full-dimensional germ, and the rank bound \(r\) no longer constrains the deployed update.
coord_notes.base_point: At \(B=0\) the coordinated delta is \(\mathrm{Dec}(H(0))\neq0\) (default nn.Linear biases), so \(\rho(q_0)\neq\theta_0\): a defect, with entries of order \(1/\sqrt{128}\). The paper's bias-free formula would start at \(\theta_0\). Under the paper's bias-free Sec. 3.3 formula (\(\sigma(0)=0\), no decoder bias) the start would be pointed but first-order deficient (only \(B\) moves at \(B=0\)): an apex. All other coordinates are the same for the paper's formula and the code.
coord_notes.gauge: The decoder alone has \(129\max d_{out}d_{in}\) entries, far more than the adapted boxes, and the GELU message layer leaves no linear group acting on the whole fibre: non-linear. The gated part alone has SoRA's fibre \(r^2+r\).
coord_notes.covariance: The image is the whole adapted box, so \(GL\times GL\). Flatten-and-pad aligns coordinates across boxes of different shapes; that matters for the dynamics, not for the image.
coord_notes.merge: The coordinated delta is one static matrix per box.
coord_notes.rebasing: The image is already the whole box, so cycles gain nothing.

methods.categorical_reading: As released, StructLoRA is not a low-rank method. The training-only coordinator's decoder is a dense trainable map back into weight space, and its output is what gets merged, so the deployed update ranges over every adapted box and starts at a defect. Only with the coordinator off (App. E.7, or merge_structlora called without a coordinator) is the object SoRA's gated cone \(W_0+\{B\,\mathrm{diag}(m)A\}\) pointed at the \(\mathrm T_A\) apex. In that reading the GCN smoothing is a training device that \(\rho\) does not see.

The released coordinated instance has no such arrow (see the obstruction).
Gated instance only, pointed at (0, A_0).

coord_notes.kind: The global object is one LoRA\(_r\) pair kept across rounds. Clients train from the previous global factors, and the contribution is the aggregation map, a training procedure on this object (as HetLoRA).
coord_notes.shape: LoRA's cone \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\); the averaged pair stays rank \(r\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(\bar B^0\bar A^0=0\) (Algorithm 1), with LoRA's \(B=0\): the \(\mathrm T_A\) apex.
coord_notes.gauge: \(\rho\) has \(GL_r\) fibres. Each client fixes the \(SO(r)\) part by Procrustes against last round's global factors (softened by \(\lambda\)). The \(\mathrm{Sym}_r\) part stays free, so factor averaging is still bilinear and not a function of the client adapters \(B_iA_i\) (Prop V.4(a,b)). \(\lambda=0\) is FedIT.
coord_notes.covariance: The image is LoRA's cone, \(GL\times GL\). The aggregation is less covariant: the Procrustes rotation minimises Frobenius distances between factors, \(\|R^\top A_i-\bar A\|_F\) and \(\|B_iR-\bar B\|_F\), which are invariant under \(A\mapsto Ah^{-1}\), \(B\mapsto gB\) only for \(h\in CO(n)\), \(g\in CO(m)\). The aggregation rule is therefore \(CO\times CO\)-equivariant, which does not affect the image.
coord_notes.merge: \(\bar B\bar A\) is an ordinary rank-\(r\) LoRA.
coord_notes.rebasing: As LoRA; the global adapter is not merged between rounds.

methods.categorical_reading: FedRot-LoRA is FedIT with a partial gauge fixing: before uploading, each client replaces \((B_i,A_i)\) by the representative of its \(SO(r)\)-orbit closest to the previous global pair. This removes the rotational part of the aggregation error \(\bar B\bar A-\tfrac1N\sum_iB_iA_i\), but not the part coming from the non-compact half of \(GL_r\). That is why Prop V.4 needs a shared factor (FFA-LoRA), stacking (FLoRA) or a gauge-invariant statistic (FLoRG) for exactness.

arrows.note: The global pair is a LoRA_r point, pointed at (0, A_0); only the aggregation differs.

obstructions.reason: d(LoRA_r) = r(m+n-r) > rm = d(FFA-LoRA): both factors train, so the row space moves.

methods.categorical_reading: LoRA-RLPO/RLMO is LoRA pointed in the \(\mathrm T_A\) stratum at the top or bottom right singular subspace of \(W_0\): PiSSA's and MiLoRA's subspaces with their Type II split removed. That puts the start back at the apex and keeps \(\|I-A_0^\top A_0\|_2=1\), the quantity in the paper's bound on the LoRA-to-full-FT gap. Every \(A_0\) with singular values \(\le\sqrt2\) attains that bound, so the orthonormal frame is one point of a large set of equally good pointings.

arrows.note: Pointed isomorphism onto LoRA_r pointed at (0, V_{[:,1:r]}^T) (resp. (0, V_{[:,-r:]}^T)). Into LoRA with a random A_0 there is only a weak morphism (a different point of Gr(r,n)).

obstructions.reason: Same top-r subspace, but RLPO is a Type I apex (B_0 = 0, W_0 unsplit) and PiSSA a Type II smooth point: different strata, incomparable images at equal rank (Thm II.2(d)).
RLMO against MiLoRA: the same bottom-r subspace, Type I apex against Type II split.
Both are T_A points, but RLPO's row A_0 is a weight frame and EVA's an activation frame. For generic data S_1 = {X V_r^T} and {X V_act^T} are not nested, so there is no pointed arrow either way.

coord_notes.kind: A \(T\)-point over the noise level \(T=[0,1]\): \(\lambda\mapsto(B,\,I_r+\eta\mathcal F_\phi(e_\lambda),\,A)\), with one hypernetwork shared by all modules.
coord_notes.shape: Each fibre \(W_0+BC(\lambda)A\) is a point of LoRA's cone, and for fixed \((B,A)\) all fibres share \(\mathrm{col}\,B\) and \(\mathrm{row}\,A\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(B=0\) and a zero-initialised last layer (\(C=I_r\)): every fibre is the \(\mathrm T_A\) apex with \(S_1=\{XA_0\}\), and the hypernetwork gets no first-order gradient (zero-gate lemma).
coord_notes.gauge: \((B_j,A_j)\mapsto(B_jG^{-1},HA_j)\) for all modules at once, with \(C(\lambda)\mapsto GC(\lambda)H^{-1}\) absorbed by the shared hypernetwork's linear last layer (weights and bias), plus one relative scalar per extra module: \(GL_r\times GL_r\times(\mathbb R^\times)^{M-1}\). Generic fibre \(2r^2+1\) for two modules (checked).
coord_notes.covariance: Fibrewise LoRA's basis-free cone.
coord_notes.merge: For fixed \(\lambda\) the fibre fuses. \(\lambda\) changes every denoising step, so the merge is per fibre (as Text-to-LoRA per task).
coord_notes.rebasing: Undefined for a family whose fibre changes with \(\lambda\).

methods.categorical_reading: NaRA is a section of LoRA over the noise-level line: a smooth map \(\lambda\mapsto W_0+BC(\lambda)A\) whose fibres move inside one fixed pair of rank-\(r\) column and row spaces, with an \(r\times r\) core produced by one hypernetwork for all modules. Static LoRA is the constant section (\(\eta=0\)). Fibrewise it is MoSLoRA with the mixer generated, and tied across modules.

arrows.note: Fibrewise over noise levels, into LoRA_r pointed at (0, A_0); pointed because B starts at 0.
Fibrewise, into MoSLoRA re-pointed at (0, I_r/s, A_0), with s MoSLoRA's scale. Its default random-mixer pointing differs, but S_1 = {XA_0} on both sides.

obstructions.reason: A rank-one fibre update uv^T lies in HiRA_r's image only if (uv^T) / W_0 (entrywise) = D_u (1/W_0) D_v has rank <= r, which fails for generic W_0 when r < min(m,n).

coord_notes.kind: A family over tokens (n-gram windows): \(\Delta W(x)=\mathrm{diag}(\mathcal P(x)+\gamma p_s)\,BA\) for LiME-LoRA, with a parameter-free router that reads the first \(E\) coordinates of \(W_0x\) and of \(\hat z\).
coord_notes.shape: Token-dependent output scalings of one shared adapter: no single weight-space image.
coord_notes.base_point: \(B=0\) gives \(\hat z=0\) and the frozen function at every token (neutral). The router's normalisation \(\hat z_{1:E}/\|\hat z_{1:E}\|_\infty\) is \(0/0\) there, so routing is undefined at the base point itself.
coord_notes.gauge: \(GL_r\) on the rank wire; the torus \((B,p_i,p_s)\mapsto(DB,D^{-1}p_i,D^{-1}p_s)\) with \(D_{1:E}=cI\), \(c>0\) (the router sees \(\hat z_{1:E}\) only up to positive scale); \((\gamma,p_s)\mapsto(c\gamma,p_s/c)\); and the translation \((p_i,p_s)\mapsto(p_i+v,\,p_s-v/\gamma)\), since the routing weights sum to 1. Fibre \(r^2+(d_{out}-E+1)+1+d_{out}\) (checked with a dense router). Nearest key GL × torus.
coord_notes.covariance: The Hadamard output scalings allow at most Mon on the output side, and the router reads the fixed first \(E\) output coordinates of \(W_0x\) and \(\hat z\), so only permutations fixing \(\{1,\dots,E\}\) survive: imposed structure \(\Pi\) (Lemma VI.2 test). GL on the input side.
coord_notes.merge: Thm VI.3 for routed mixtures: the scaling changes per token. M1 only for \(E=1\).
coord_notes.rebasing: Undefined: not mergeable.

methods.categorical_reading: LiME is an \(X\)-point of row scalings of one shared LoRA update: MoV's routed scaling vectors, moved from \(W_0\) to the adapter's output. Per token its weight \(W_0+\mathrm{diag}(v(x))BA\) lies in LoRA\(_r\) with a fixed row space and a token-dependent column space \(\mathrm{diag}(v(x))\,\mathrm{col}\,B\). The router borrows coordinates of \(W_0x\) and \(\hat z\) as logits. That is what makes it parameter-free, and also what fixes a privileged output basis.

arrows.note: Fibrewise over tokens, into LoRA_r pointed at (0, A_0). Piecewise smooth only: h_x is smooth where the selected set S_theta(x) is locally constant and z-hat_{1:E}(x) != 0. At q_0 (B = 0) the router is 0/0; h_x is continuous there with h_x(q_0) = (0, A_0), because P(x) is a convex combination and hence bounded, but it is not differentiable (the infinity-norm normalisation flips with the sign of B). At q_0 the arrow certifies the inclusion of each realised fibre in Im LoRA_r rather than a smooth pointed morphism.

obstructions.reason: Per token both have the form (mixture of heads) times a shared A, but LiME's confidence-adaptive top-k (theta = 0.7) and n-gram windows switch experts discontinuously, while HydraLoRA's dense softmax gates are continuous in the token. So for generic trained parameters LiME's routed functions are not HydraLoRA's (the MixLoRA argument).

coord_notes.kind: Forward map \(\mathrm{id}_\Theta\). The gradient is replaced by a one-sided finite difference along \(\Delta_\ell=R_\ell U_\ell^\top\), where \(U_\ell\) is the top activation subspace found by power iteration in the same forward pass: compression \(g\mapsto\langle\Delta,g\rangle\), anchor \(\lambda\mapsto\lambda\Delta\).
coord_notes.shape: Each step is the line \(\theta_t+\mathbb R\Delta_t\) (\(d=1\)), with \(\Delta_t\) of rank \(\le r\) per matrix (\(r=1\)) and its row space in the current activation subspace.
coord_notes.base_point: No reparametrisation; each step is a linear method at its own base.
coord_notes.gauge: None.
coord_notes.covariance: \(R_\ell\) is Gaussian (output side, \(O(m)\) in law) and \(U_\ell\) an activation frame (\(CO(n)\), data): covariance holds only in law.
coord_notes.merge: Writes \(W\) directly; nothing to merge.
coord_notes.rebasing: A rebasing scheme of lines resampled every step. The reach is \(\Theta\): \(R_\ell\) is resampled and the activation frames move with the data.

methods.categorical_reading: AGZO is MeZO with its random line restricted to the slice \(\{XU_\ell^\top\}\), which contains the row space of every layer gradient \(Q_\ell H_\ell^\top\). The compression is still one directional derivative, but along a rank-\(r\) direction whose input side is a data frame. Per step it is LoRA-FA\((U_\ell^\top)\) along a single random line, re-based every step.

arrows.note: Per step at base theta_t: the line theta_t + lambda R_t U_t^T is a line of LoRA-FA(A_0 := U_t^T), pointed at 0. Linear layers only: AGZO's dense Gaussian perturbation of the other parameters (norms, biases, embeddings) lies outside LoRA-FA's boxes.

obstructions.reason: Per step, AGZO's direction R U^T has rank <= r on every linear layer, while MeZO's Gaussian direction has full rank almost surely. So the step lines differ, and AGZO's line is not in MeZO's. Read in law: the rank-<=r directions form a measure-zero set that MeZO's Gaussian direction hits with probability 0.

methods.check_notes: Independent check 2026-10-02: coordinates confirmed (MeZO precedent: B / moving line / regular / none / frame / null / schedule). Arrow note qualified to linear layers (the other parameters get dense Gaussian perturbations); obstruction note made explicit as a statement in law. coord_notes.kind: Forward map \(\mathrm{id}_\Theta\): multi-query forward differences in a random column-orthonormal left frame \(P_\ell\) (resampled every 100 steps), a matrix sign on the \(r\times d_{in}\) estimate, and the anchor \(Z\mapsto P_\ell Z\).
coord_notes.shape: Per period the linear space \(\{W_k+P_kX\}\), \(d=rd_{in}\), as GaLore with a random projector (left side). The matrix sign changes the step within the period, not the period's image.
coord_notes.base_point: Each period is a linear method at its own base.
coord_notes.gauge: None.
coord_notes.covariance: Haar \(P_\ell\) on the output side and Gaussian queries on the input side: covariance in law.
coord_notes.merge: Writes \(W\) directly; nothing to merge.
coord_notes.rebasing: Moving random left frames: a rebasing scheme reaching \(\Theta\).

methods.categorical_reading: ZO-Muon is the zeroth-order version of a one-sided GaLore period with a random frame: per period it is FB\((P_k)\), the frozen-\(B\) sub-object of LoRA, trained by forward differences and orthogonalised steps. The subspace is what makes the matrix sign useful, since it then acts on an \(r\times d_{in}\) estimate whose variance scales with \(rd_{in}\) rather than \(d_{out}d_{in}\).

arrows.note: Per period at base W_k: FB(P_k) is LoRA with B frozen at P_k, pointed at (P_k, 0) (stratum T_B), as for GaLore's left-projection case and Online Subspace Descent. Weight matrices only; 1-D parameters (biases, norms) get dense Gaussian RGE and lie outside the frozen-B slice.

obstructions.reason: Per period, a Haar-random frame P_k against GaLore's gradient-SVD frame: the period images are generically not nested.
A ZO-Muon period has d = r d_in > 1, the dimension of a MeZO step line.

methods.check_notes: Independent check 2026-10-02: coordinates confirmed (GaLore-with-random-projector precedent; the released code puts P on the output side). A2 arrow FB(P_k) -> LoRA at a T_B point is exact; note qualified to weight matrices. Obstructions against GaLore (frames generically not nested) and MeZO (O2, per-period dimension r d_in > 1) accepted. coord_notes.kind: AdaLoRA's \(P\Lambda Q\) parametrisation with a soft orthogonality penalty. Ranks move between matrices by a spectral-entropy score: pruned triplets are dropped and new ones appended at \(\lambda=0\).
coord_notes.shape: Per matrix \(W_0+\{P\Lambda Q\}=W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r_\ell}\). With moving \(r_\ell\) the trained object is a union, over allocations with \(\sum_\ell r_\ell\) fixed, of products of cones.
coord_notes.base_point: \(\Lambda_0=0\) with \(P,Q\sim\mathcal N(0,0.02^2)\): \(S_1=\mathrm{span}\{p_iq_i^\top\}\), \(\dim S_1=r_\ell\), as AdaLoRA. Expansion at \(\lambda=0\) re-enters this apex for the new direction, so growth is function-preserving.
coord_notes.gauge: AdaLoRA's fibre \(r(r+1)\): non-linear (two torus edges plus absorption of \(\Lambda\)).
coord_notes.covariance: The score is a function of \(\Lambda\) only, and the image is LoRA's: basis-free.
coord_notes.merge: \(P_\ell\Lambda_\ell Q_\ell\) fuses.
coord_notes.rebasing: As AdaLoRA: \(\to\Theta\).

methods.categorical_reading: FlexLoRA is AdaLoRA's object with a different budget dynamic. Rank leaves matrices whose learned spectrum \(\Lambda_\ell\) is concentrated and enters matrices whose spectrum is spread, moving between nested sub-cones (A2 truncations) and their \(\lambda=0\) extensions (A5 stages). Because the score reads \(\Lambda\) alone, it inherits the gauge dependence of \(P\Lambda Q\): \(\Lambda\) equals the singular values of \(\Delta W\) only when the orthogonality penalty is exactly satisfied.

arrows.note: The same P Lambda Q object pointed at Lambda = 0 with the same frames, at any fixed allocation; only the rank schedule differs.
The same object; both prune and expand inside the rank filtration, with different scores.
Pointed at (0, Q_0).

obstructions.reason: dim S_1(FlexLoRA) = r (Lambda_0 = 0), while DyLoRA's S_1 = {XA_0} is m r-dimensional and does not contain span{p_i q_i^T} for generic frames: no pointed arrow at the default pointings.

The DyLoRA O3 obstruction was re-checked numerically: p_i q_i^T has relative residual 0.43 outside {X A_0} for generic frames, so S_1 is not contained. Arrows into AdaLoRA, ElaLoRA (h = id at a fixed allocation and the same frames) and LoRA ((P Lambda, Q), pointed at (0, Q_0)) are exact. coord_notes.kind: A family over tokens: top-\(k\) routing over \(Z\) spectral experts, \(\Delta W(x)=\eta\sum_{i\in\mathcal S(x)}g_i(x)\,\mathcal F^{-1}(E_i)\).
coord_notes.shape: A token-dependent mixture: no single weight-space image. Each expert is a fixed-support linear map of its complex coefficients (rank \(\le2\) per conjugate pair).
coord_notes.base_point: Not specified, and no code. Read at the exactly pointed variant (zero coefficients, the convention used for FourierFT): every expert is \(0\), the frozen function at every token (neutral), and the router gets no first-order gradient. A FourierFT-style \(\mathcal N(0,1)\) start would be a defect.
coord_notes.gauge: Per expert none, \(+1\) per self-conjugate frequency (dead imaginary part) and \(+2\) per conjugate pair sampled twice (complex coefficients \(c_1,c_2\) at \((u,v)\) and \((-u,-v)\) enter only through \(c_1+\bar c_2\); FourierFT's real coefficients give \(+1\)). The router's softmax translation is a kernel-type redundancy (as for MoV).
coord_notes.covariance: The Fourier frame imposes a cyclic order on both sides (\(\Pi_{\rm cyc}\), as FourierFT); the router is dense on the input.
coord_notes.merge: Routing changes per token; M1 only with frozen routing.
coord_notes.rebasing: Undefined: not mergeable.

methods.categorical_reading: FourierMoE is an \(X\)-point of a complex-coefficient FourierFT: the router chooses, per token, which frequency bands the update uses. Learning the phase as well as the amplitude takes each expert out of FourierFT's point-symmetric subspace \(\Delta W_{j,l}=\Delta W_{-j,-l}\) (the sine patterns are point-antisymmetric), so the experts share FourierFT's frame but are not FourierFT experts. Fibrewise the method still factors through LoRA-FA with a frozen trigonometric input frame.

arrows.note: Fibrewise over tokens, into LoRA-FA(A_F) with the frozen input frame A_F = [cos phi_k; sin phi_k] over the union of the experts' supports. Here c_k = a_k + i b_k, and theta_k, phi_k are the output and input phase vectors of frequency (u_k, v_k); the factor is 1 instead of 2 for self-conjugate frequencies. Pointed at 0 for the zero-coefficient pointing. Checked numerically (2e-17). As for routed mixtures in general, the top-k selection makes h_x only piecewise smooth in the router parameters; it is smooth in the coefficients c_i, and h_x(q_0) = 0 for every router value.

obstructions.reason: A complex coefficient c = a + ib contributes -2b sin(theta + phi), a point-antisymmetric pattern. FourierFT's real spectrum keeps every update in the point-symmetric subspace Delta W_{j,l} = Delta W_{-j,-l}, so no expert with b != 0, and no routed mixture of such experts, lies in FourierFT's image. Checked numerically.

methods.check_notes: Independent check 2026-10-02: doubt resolved and verified set to true: the base point is coded at the exactly pointed variant (zero coefficients), the framework's convention for implementations that do not start at theta_0 (Table VIII.B footnote), with the N(0,1) FourierFT-style start recorded as a defect alternative; the parameter-count mismatch is upstream and affects no coordinate. CORRECTED the gauge note: a conjugate pair sampled twice gives +2, not +1, with complex coefficients (numpy Jacobian rank 2 of 4); a self-conjugate frequency gives +1 (rank 1 of 2). Re-checked with numpy: the expert IDFT is real, it equals B(c) A_F with the trigonometric frame (1.4e-16), real spectra give point-symmetric updates and imaginary parts point-antisymmetric ones (1.6e-17), so the FourierFT obstruction holds. Added the piecewise-smoothness caveat (top-k router) to the LoRA-FA arrow. Classifier note: Classified 2026-10-02 from addendum2026-2. No public code and no stated initialisation; base point coded at the exactly pointed variant (neutral), following the FourierFT convention. The LoRA-FA factorisation and the antisymmetry obstruction were checked numerically. Unresolved upstream: the paper's trainable-parameter count does not match its hyperparameters.

coord_notes.kind: An additive update on \(W_0\), Hadamard-modulated by \(W_0\) itself.
coord_notes.shape: \(\Delta W=(P_{out}^\top\tilde B\tilde AP_{in})\odot W_0\) (checked): \((D_{W_0})_*\) of a block-diagonal LoRA (MELoRA's shape) in coordinates permuted once from the SVD of \(W_0\). A transported product of \(K\) block cones of rank \(r/K\), inside HiRA\(_r\)'s image.
coord_notes.base_point: Not stated. With HiRA's zero factor (the setup the paper follows) every block is in the \(\mathrm T_A\) stratum: an apex, with MELoRA's deficit \(\sum_k\tfrac rK(\tfrac{d_{in}}K-\tfrac rK)\) carried by the transport.
coord_notes.gauge: \(\prod_{k=1}^KGL_{r/K}\); the transport preserves it.
coord_notes.covariance: The Hadamard factor gives HiRA's Mon×Mon, and the SVD-derived ordering is covariant under signed permutations and homotheties but not under non-uniform diagonal scalings: nearest key MonxMon. If the grouping rule were not permutation-equivariant (the paper does not state it), the block partition would be an imposed structure (\(\Pi\)).
coord_notes.merge: The scattered-back \(\Delta W\) is one dense matrix.
coord_notes.rebasing: With the permutations frozen, \((1+X)\odot Y\) stays block-diagonal, so \(R_\infty=W_0+W_0\odot\{\text{block-diagonal in permuted coordinates}\}\): off-diagonal blocks and the zeros of \(W_0\) never move. The span of the shape, not \(\Theta\).

methods.categorical_reading: SMoA is MELoRA transported by HiRA's \(\theta_0\)-dependent Hadamard frame \(D_{W_0}\), after a spectral reordering of rows and columns; equivalently, HiRA\(_r\) with block-sparse factors. Its rank ceiling exceeds LoRA's, but at budget \(r\) its update set is a subset of HiRA\(_r\)'s, reached with \(1/K\) of the parameters. So its gain over HiRA is in parameter count, not expressivity.

arrows.note: Into HiRA_r pointed at (0, blkdiag(A_{k,0}) P_in), a T_A point (zero-factor init assumed). Checked numerically (exact).

obstructions.reason: max rank sum_k min(s_k, (r/K) rank M_k) > r (Prop. 1).

MELoRA's block-diagonal updates are additive in the standard coordinates; SMoA's are W_0-modulated blocks in permuted coordinates, which keep the zeros of W_0 and use a different partition. Neither image contains the other. At equal budget the rank argument also applies: an SMoA block (B_k A_k) . M_k has rank up to min(s_k, rho rank M_k) = s_k for generic W_0 (numerically 6 against r = 4 at 8 x 6, K = 2), while every MELoRA block has rank <= r/K.

methods.check_notes: Independent check 2026-10-02: doubts resolved and verified set to true: the base point is coded at HiRA's zero-factor init, which the paper says it follows (exactly pointed variant per the framework's convention), and covariance MonxMon holds on the assumption, stated in the note, that the SVD-based grouping rule is permutation-equivariant (otherwise Pi). Re-checked with numpy: the Hadamard rewriting Delta W = (P_out^T B~ A~ P_in) . W_0 is exact (0.0), the HiRA arrow holds (1e-17) and rank Delta W = 6 > r = 4 (O2 against LoRA). Rebasing 'span' (R_infinity = W_0 + W_0 . {block-diagonal}, frozen permutations) re-derived. Added a rank argument to the MELoRA obstruction. The Hadamard rewriting and the HiRA arrow were checked numerically. The permutation rule is unspecified, which leaves covariance between MonxMon and Pi.

coord_notes.kind: A family over a noise base, trained jointly by an ELBO (as BLoB). Both factors are sampled from Kronecker sparse-GP conditionals \(T_rUT_c\) plus noise of scale \(\lambda\), with a flow posterior on the inducing matrices.
coord_notes.shape: Every sample, and the posterior mean, lies in LoRA's cone \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r_L}\).
coord_notes.base_point: Released code: inducing means \(\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\) and random locations make both sampled factors nonzero at step 0, so \(\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA\neq0\): a small defect. The unused InducingAdapter wrapper with zero output scale would have been neutral.
coord_notes.gauge: The factors are rational in \((Z,D,U)\) through \(K^{-1}\). The rank-wire \(GL_{r_L}\) lifts to these coordinates only in its orthogonal part, and the generic fibre is not a linear-group orbit: non-linear.
coord_notes.covariance: The image is LoRA's (\(GL\times GL\)). The diagonal noise and diagonal \(D\) make the distribution itself only Mon-covariant.
coord_notes.merge: The posterior mean fuses (deterministic mode). The calibrated predictive averages \(N=4\) sampled adapters at test time, so it is M\(\infty\) (as BLoB).
coord_notes.rebasing: Undefined: the calibrated object does not merge.

methods.categorical_reading: Bayesian-LoRA is a family over a noise space whose samples are LoRA points with both factors random, generated from small inducing matrices through a bilinear GP conditional \(T_rUT_c\) that has LoRA's own shape. Its mean projects to a LoRA point (Corollary 4.2). Its distribution, however, lives on \(Q\) through a parametrisation that is not gauge-invariant, so the calibrated uncertainty depends on the factor representative, as for Laplace-LoRA.

arrows.h: h=\big(\bar B,\ \bar A\big),\ \ \bar B=T_r^B\,\mathbb E_q[U^B]\,T_c^B,\ \ \bar A=T_r^A\,\mathbb E_q[U^A]\,T_c^A
arrows.note: Projection to the posterior mean (B and A are independent, so E[BA] = B-bar A-bar), scales absorbed. Pointed at h(q_0), which is not LoRA's B = 0 pointing because the released init is a defect, so the arrow lives in the unpointed slice.

obstructions.reason: BLoB's samples keep the trained col B, since its B is deterministic. Bayesian-LoRA samples B as well, so its posterior support leaves every fixed FB(B) slice.

methods.check_notes: Independent check 2026-10-02: coordinates confirmed (BLoB / Laplace-LoRA precedent; defect from the released InducingLinear init). The posterior-mean arrow is exact because A and B are independent under q, so E[BA] = E[B]E[A]; it lives in the unpointed slice. Gauge 'nonlinear' is accepted on inspection: under Z -> GZ the kernel K = ZZ^T + D^2 stays of the same form only for G preserving the diagonal D^2, so no GL_r lifts; no Jacobian check was possible without fixing which map is rho for a noise family. BLoB obstruction confirmed. Classifier note: Classified 2026-10-02 from addendum2026-2 (released code as recorded there: InducingLinear layers replace both LoRA factors, random init). Precedents: BLoB and Laplace-LoRA (F_T over a noise base, Cone, GLxGL image, Minf, null). Gauge coded nonlinear by inspection of the rational parametrisation, not by a Jacobian check.

coord_notes.kind: A single trained factor in \(W_0+LA^\top AR\) with frozen semi-orthogonal frames. The federation averages the Gram core \(A^\top A\) and re-factors it every round.

methods.categorical_reading: GiVA is VeRA with its frozen random pair replaced by a task-informed one. It has the same toric cone of dimension \(d_{out}+r-1\), now inside LoRA-FA\((V_r^\top)\) with the gradient's dominant right singular frame, which makes the one-sided first-order step \(GA^\top A\) the best rank-\(r\) approximation of \(G\). The gain over VeRA is in the frame, not the shape: the fixed row space is chosen rather than drawn.

coord_notes.covariance: The prompt is a full vector at every position of the wire, carried to itself by every linear function-preserving gauge of that wire. Positions are the network's own tokens or pixels, not an imposed frame: function-level GL×GL. VP's border frame is what makes VP \(\Pi\).

methods.categorical_reading: Activation prompting inserts a single translation box on the activation wire at layer \(l\), neutral at zero. Input-level additive VP is the case \(l=0\), and a position-uniform \(\delta\) is a bias edit, which is why Proposition 1 can match it with shift-only normalisation tuning at that layer. Its position resolution is what keeps it from being a weight-space method; its depth changes only how far the backward pass must reach.

arrows.note: Position-uniform instance only (the hypothesis of Prop. 1), on a ViT whose residual stream at layer l is last written by the biased MLP output projection of block l-1: the shift is that bias edit, BitFit pointed at 0. The released position-specific delta has no such arrow (M-infinity).

obstructions.reason: f(theta_0) is AP's value at delta = 0, while no VPT parameter reproduces f (extra tokens always draw attention mass), so Im AP is not inside Im VPT.

LayerNorm shifts are shared across positions; a position-specific delta at one layer is not a (gamma, beta) edit. Prop. 1's matching needs a position-uniform delta, unit effective scale and batch-invariant statistics.

methods.categorical_reading: Stable-LoRA is LoRA with a transient change of trained-method data: an early decay of \(A\), independent of the learning rate, that removes the long-term imprint of a nonzero \(A_0\) on width scaling, after which training is plain AdamW. As an object it is LoRA. Like LoRA+ (rates) and LoRA-RITE (preconditioner), all of its content is in the trajectory.

coord_notes.kind: The deployed object: the LayerNorm affine parameters of every backbone block plus a new head. The ladder side network, bottlenecks and generator are training-only teachers and are discarded.

methods.categorical_reading: MDPD is LN-tuning reached through a different training signal. A side network (LST-type, an unpointed extension) is trained on the task and mutually distilled with the frozen backbone, and only the backbone's norm parameters and a head survive. The side network lives entirely on the cotangent side: it shapes the gradient that the selective block receives, which the deployed object cannot see.

arrows.note: The same deployed object (LayerNorm (gamma, beta) of every block, with the same new task head on both sides); only the training signal differs.

obstructions.reason: The frozen backbone function (pretrained norm parameters, with the same head on both sides) is in Im MDPD, while LST is unpointed: its side network's up-projection has rank <= d/r, so no LST parameter reproduces it. So Im MDPD is not inside Im LST. LST also keeps its side network at inference.
